wayricad.name: WayriCAD
wayricad.summary: Follow PCB selections into PI/SI studies, review explicit power paths and explore bounded AC impedance models, with more reliable thermal solves.
changes: Quick PI and Quick SI follow idle PCB selection with explicit source/load roles and saved-geometry checks. Power-path diagrams and named bundle cases make the study setup easier to review.
Two separate AC tools cover straight rectangular-conductor MQS two-port impedance and an explicitly meshed quasi-TEM planar PDN cavity. Each retains its own return-path and geometry assumptions.
QuickTherm includes known source power when no sources are selected, handles compatible shared-cell temperature fixtures, and improves sparse-solve and radiation-step reliability.
Optional Windows CalculiX setup can provision a pinned, checksum-verified solver. Explicit solver paths and offline operation remain available.
Portable Web Export retains saved-source freshness checks and separate original/embedded hashes; its bundled WebView version is independently pinned.
wayricad.note: Selection following uses saved geometry. Power-path previews are topology, not solved results. AC models have explicit conductor/reference-plane limits; thermal changes improve solver reliability without establishing measured accuracy.

spike.name: SPIKE
spike.summary: A clearer power-tree overview and a Geometry → basic PI handoff to the existing PCB resistive-network solver.
changes: Power-tree branches have direction, collapse, fit and zoom, with selection and evidence details. Inferred electrical paths still need review.
Geometry → basic PI passes normalized PCB copper to the existing routed DC solver and returns geometry-linked fields; it does not infer electrical properties from arbitrary STEP solids.
Saved thermal studies reopen in thermal setup. Workspace search, board-net controls and axis rotation rings have been refined.
spike.note: This source-only hotfix adds no installer or numerical kernel. Numerical review remains incomplete and the full Python suite does not pass; use the release record for the exact limits.

kicad_online.name: KiCad Online
kicad_online.summary: Read saved drawing details more faithfully, navigate repeated sheets and inspect multilayer boards without losing the selected net.
changes: Scoped text variables, embedded symbol overrides, sheet-pin markers, supported images and internal sheet links follow the saved drawing.
Repeated sheet instances have readable explorer rows and a shared hierarchy map. Selected-net connectivity refreshes as sheets load.
Inner copper can be isolated and restored. Expanded 3D inspection keeps saved artwork and substrate materials; selected copper keeps its layer colors and vias remain gold.
Review comments use a simpler placement toolbar, severity bubbles and corrected capture offsets. Website-session replies retain their conversation context.
Metadata parsing reuses board data and reduces retained geometry in project caches; the release makes no universal memory or device-speed guarantee.
kicad_online.note: GitHub preview and store versions can differ; recorded channel states are listed below. Android 1.100 is a development-signed, manually updated GitHub APK. Installed comment round trips and physical-phone acceptance remain incomplete for this version.

distribution.chrome: 0.12.101 published; 0.12.102 pending review with automatic publication

webview.name: KiCad WebView
webview.summary: Stable embed API 1.0, camera-preserving net focus and cleaner 3D rendering.
changes: Core embed API 1.0 with typed classic, ES module and lite entry points; no Node.js needed in browser embeds.
Net and pad cross-selection preserve the 3D camera. Explicit part selection still frames the mounting side.
Selected-net vias stay gold; unrelated copper, models and structure fade to gray/translucent in assembled and expanded Dim views.
Resolved copper-depth smoothing, compact inspection controls, linked sheets, results layers and source-bound project navigation.
webview.note: Read-only visualization; missing models and rendering approximations remain disclosed. Large-project acceptance ceilings do not qualify maximum-size 3D rendering, physical-phone speed or solver accuracy. Other products retain separately pinned WebView versions.
